scope: Shared calculator CSV downloads, native file sharing and local PDF generation for mobile Safari and Chrome. Local production build; not deployed.
changes: CSV download anchors are attached to the document. Blob URLs remain usable while the save link is visible, with delayed cleanup after replacement or unmount.

CSV and PDF retain an explicit Download file link if automatic downloads are blocked. Save or share is offered only when native file sharing supports the generated file; sharing runs from a fresh user tap.

PDF generation runs locally and is loaded on demand. It includes result metrics, example/current-result labeling, explanatory notes and all table rows, with repeated table headers and support for long cells.
PDF tables match selected currency precision and localized numeric formatting; CSV numeric cells remain ungrouped for spreadsheet import. Both retain the existing result display precision.
Mobile touch devices use the real PDF export. Desktop Print is retained and has a visible PDF fallback. Existing private-input export exclusions remain in place.
The seven new interface messages are translated into all seven non-English languages.

dependency.loading: Lazy client import on PDF action

unitTests.note: Initial default-concurrency runs timed out in an existing translation-rendering test. The complete suite passed with two workers; no unrelated test behavior was changed.

coverage: Complete CSV schedule and persistent retry URL
Valid multipage PDF with native printing unavailable
Native file sharing with fresh user activation; cancellation
Blocked sharing falls back to download
Blocked automatic downloads fall back to explicit save links
PDF generation failure can be retried
Hindi and Arabic PDF titles, downloads and narrow layouts

First and last pages of a 360-payment loan schedule; 13 PDF pages, including payment 360 and final zero balance
Mobile export controls and retained download link
limitations: Browser tests use desktop browser engines with mobile emulation. Native OS share menus are mocked to verify activation, file handoff, cancellation and fallback. No physical phone was connected.

PDF pages use browser-rendered images to preserve complex scripts. They are printable but do not contain selectable text; CSV provides machine-readable data. The PDF contains result metrics, notes and full tables; the existing desktop page print retains charts and article content.
